mainTopic: רב קטינא's rule about cases under a פרוטה, the משנה of the five cases of חומש, and whether רבי מאיר gives rabbinic rules like דמאי Torah-like strength.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge against רב קטינא. A ברייתא implies that repaying less than a פרוטה applies only to הקדש, so the גמרא restates his rule: a court needs a פרוטה to open a case, but it finishes the case even if the value drops below a פרוטה. Then a new משנה lists five groups of cases where a person must add a חומש, an extra fifth. רבי אלעזר is bothered that one item, תרומת מעשר של דמאי, is only rabbinic, so why would it get the Torah's חומש? רב נחמן in the name of שמואל answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that חכמים gave their rules Torah-like strength. The proof is a ברייתא about a גט brought from overseas, where רבי מאיר treats a missing rabbinic statement so seriously that a later child is a ממזר. רב ששת then challenges this from a משנה where רבי מאיר is lenient about redeeming מעשר שני of דמאי, even allowing silver to be redeemed onto copper. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse includes less than a פרוטה only for הקדש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one must return less than a פרוטה taken from הקדש. The גמרא reads this as meaning: for הקדש yes, for an ordinary person no. That challenges רב קטינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse comes to include less than a פרוטה's worth for the duty to repay. To הקדש, yes; but to an ordinary person, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא and draws an inference from it. That inference goes against what רב קטינא had said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a person must repay הקדש even for less than a פרוטה. Since this was singled out for הקדש, the גמרא infers that between ordinary people there is no such duty. That clashes with the earlier version of רב קטינא's rule, which let a court deal with cases worth less than a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: less than the value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin that counts in court
repayment, giving back what was taken
the Temple treasury, consecrated property
an ordinary person, not the Temple

phrases.english: To include less than the value of a peruta for repayment.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא reading the פסוק in ויקרא 5:16, "ואת אשר חטא מן הקדש ישלם."

phrases.english: To the Temple, yes,
but to an ordinary person, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge to רב קטינא that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version of רב קטינא's rule, that a court deals with cases worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits repaying less than a פרוטה to הקדש, so ordinary claims under a פרוטה do not have to be repaid. Then why would a court take up such a case?

steps.title: רב קטינא's rule restated: a court finishes a case that dropped below a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב קטינא. A case must be worth a פרוטה to open in court. If the value later drops below a פרוטה, the court still finishes and rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רב קטינא said: if the court took up a case worth a פרוטה, it finishes the case even if it is now worth less than a פרוטה. To start a case we need a פרוטה; to finish it we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the old version of רב קטינא's rule and gives a new, narrower version that fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new version does not say a court opens cases worth less than a פרוטה. It only says that a case properly opened at a פרוטה is finished even if the item lost value. The ברייתא's rule that ordinary claims under a פרוטה are not repaid stays in place for the start of a case.

keyTerms.meaning: if it was said, this is how it was said; the גמרא's way of restating a teaching
the court took up the case
they finish, they issue the ruling
the start of the court case
the end of the case, the verdict

steps.whatToRemember: A court needs a פרוטה to open a case, but not to close it. Once a case begins at a פרוטה, it is finished even if the value drops.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב קטינא now holds that courts open cases worth less than a פרוטה. The restated rule only covers a case that started at a full פרוטה.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rav Ketina said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הוּזְקְקוּ בֵּית דִּין לְשָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה –
phrases.english: If the court took up a case worth a peruta,
they finish it, even for less than a peruta's worth.
phrases.notes: He means the item lost value during the case and is now worth less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: For the start of the case we need a peruta,
for the end of the case we do not need a peruta.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by restating רב קטינא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the teaching in a narrower form
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב קטינא held that a court opens cases worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A court needs a פרוטה to open a case. Once the case has begun, it finishes even if the value drops below a פרוטה.

steps.title: משנה: the five kinds of cases that add a חומש
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists five kinds of cases where a person adds a חומש (an extra fifth) when paying. These are: eating holy gifts meant for a כהן, redeeming his own נטע רבעי or מעשר שני, redeeming his own הקדש, benefiting from הקדש, and robbing then swearing falsely.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are five 'fifths.' First: one who eats תרומה, תרומת מעשר, תרומת מעשר של דמאי, חלה, or ביכורים adds a fifth. Second: one who redeems his own נטע רבעי or מעשר שני adds a fifth. Third: one who redeems his own הקדש adds a fifth. Fourth: one who benefits a פרוטה's worth from הקדש adds a fifth. Fifth: one who robs his friend of a פרוטה's worth and swears falsely to him adds a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists all the cases where the halacha requires paying an extra fifth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier משנה, this one gathers cases that share one feature, here the added חומש. The count of five refers to groups. The many holy gifts for a כהן count together as one group, and נטע רבעי and מעשר שני form another. Including תרומת מעשר של דמאי in the list is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: an added fifth, paid on top of the main amount
the portion the לוי separates from his מעשר and gives to a כהן
produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it
fruit of a tree in its fourth year
one who redeems, buying back holy produce or property with money
he swore, here a false oath denying the theft

steps.whatToRemember: There are five groups where a חומש is added. Note that rabbinic תרומת מעשר של דמאי appears in the list right alongside Torah-level cases.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: There are five 'fifths,'
phrases.notes: The list seems longer than five, but it is counted in groups. All the gifts for a כהן count as one.

phrases.english: and these are they: one who eats terumah,
or terumah of the tithe,
or terumah of the tithe of demai,
or challah, or first fruits: he adds a fifth.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַפּוֹדֶה נֶטַע רְבָעִי וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלּוֹ –
phrases.english: And one who redeems his own fourth-year fruit or second tithe
adds a fifth.
One who redeems his own consecrated property adds a fifth.
One who benefits a peruta's worth from consecrated property
adds a fifth.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַגּוֹזֵל אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה וְנִשְׁבַּע לוֹ –
phrases.english: And one who robs his fellow of a peruta's worth and swears to him
adds a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In five groups of cases a person must add a חומש when paying or redeeming.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's difficulty: a חומש for rabbinic דמאי?
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that רבי אלעזר was bothered by the משנה's inclusion of תרומת מעשר של דמאי. Tithing דמאי is only rabbinic, so would חכמים really give it the strength of a Torah law by requiring a חומש?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי אלעזר found תרומת מעשר של דמאי difficult. Did חכמים strengthen their own rulings to be like Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a challenge to one item on the list, תרומת מעשר של דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חומש is a Torah penalty for eating real תרומה. דמאי must be tithed only because of a rabbinic decree, so its תרומת מעשר is rabbinic too. Requiring a חומש for it treats a rabbinic rule as if it were Torah law, and רבי אלעזר asks whether חכמים would do that.

keyTerms.meaning: he found it difficult
did the Sages strengthen their own rulings?
like the laws of the Torah

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said:
Rabbi Elazar found difficult
the terumah of the tithe of demai:
Did the Sages give their words extra strength
phrases.notes: Tithing דמאי is only a rabbinic rule, so he is surprised it gets the Torah's חומש.

phrases.english: like those of the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one item in the משנה of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who eats תרומת מעשר של דמאי adds a חומש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דמאי is only a rabbinic obligation, and חכמים do not usually give their own rulings the full force of Torah law, such as the חומש penalty.

steps.title: Our משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל answers that the משנה is the view of רבי מאיר, who holds חכמים strengthened their rules like Torah rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי מאיר, who says the Sages strengthened their words to be like Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אלעזר's question from Step 4. It says the משנה that requires a חומש for rabbinic דמאי follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: would חכמים really treat a rabbinic rule with the strength of a Torah law? The answer is that רבי מאיר holds exactly that, so the משנה follows him. The other חכמים may not agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A way of naming which תנא a source follows
The Sages gave strength to their own rules
Like those of the Torah

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה requiring a חומש for תרומת מעשר של דמאי.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר עָשׂוּ חֲכָמִים חִיזּוּק לְדִבְרֵיהֶם כְּשֶׁל תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: who says: the Sages gave their words strength like the words of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's difficulty by naming the תנא behind the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא (רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nobody would give a rabbinic rule like דמאי the strength of Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר does give rabbinic rules Torah-like strength, and the משנה follows him.

steps.title: Proof from a גט brought from overseas
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר treating a rabbinic requirement for a גט so strictly that a later child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: If someone brings a גט from overseas and gives it to her without saying 'It was written and signed in my presence,' a man who marries her must divorce her, and the child is a ממזר, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say the child is not a ממזר. What should be done? He takes it back from her and gives it again in front of two people, and says 'It was written and signed in my presence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי מאיר strengthens rabbinic rules. Saying "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם" is only a rabbinic rule, yet he treats skipping it very seriously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Torah law the גט is fine even if the messenger did not make that statement. Still, רבי מאיר says that if she remarries, the child is a ממזר, as if the divorce never took effect. The חכמים disagree about the child, but they also want the messenger to fix it by giving it again with the statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Overseas, any land outside ארץ ישראל
"It was written in my presence and signed in my presence", a declaration the messenger must make
He must divorce her (send her out)
A child born from a forbidden union such as adultery

steps.confusionAlert: The ממזר status is not about the first husband. It is about a child born if she remarries relying on this גט.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas,
gave it to her but did not say to her:
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"
he must divorce her, and the child is a mamzer,
phrases.notes: "He" is a new husband who married her based on this גט.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: the child is not a mamzer.
How should he proceed?

phrases.aramaic: יִטְּלֶנּוּ מִמֶּנָּה וְיַחֲזוֹר וְיִתְּנֶנּוּ לָהּ בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: He should take it from her and give it to her again in front of two people,
and say to her: "It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source showing רבי מאיר's principle claimed in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר gives rabbinic rules Torah-like strength
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about a גט brought from overseas without the statement בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם

steps.title: Is רבי מאיר really that strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: just for missing a rabbinic statement, does רבי מאיר really say she must be divorced and the child is a ממזר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר, just because he did not say 'It was written and signed in my presence,' must he divorce her and the child is a ממזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expresses surprise at how extreme רבי מאיר's ruling in the ברייתא sounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט is valid under Torah law, and only a rabbinic statement was missing. Making the child a ממזר for that seems far too harsh, so the גמרא asks whether this can really be his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Just because he did not say

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir,
just because he did not say to her
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence",
he must divorce her and the child is a mamzer?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא אָמַר לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the harshness of רבי מאיר's ruling quoted in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling in the ברייתא of the גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Missing a mere rabbinic statement should not make a child a ממזר.

steps.title: Yes, this is רבי מאיר's consistent view
steps.stepSummary: Yes. רבי מאיר holds that anyone who changes the formula חכמים set for גיטין causes a forced divorce and a ממזר child.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning, as רב המנונא said in the name of עולא: רבי מאיר would say, anyone who changes from the formula חכמים set for גיטין, he must divorce her and the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms that רבי מאיר really is this strict, and shows it is his general rule for גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a one-time ruling. רבי מאיר consistently says that any change from the חכמים' set formula for a גט has these results. That supports the idea that he gives rabbinic rules Torah-like strength, which also explains the חומש for דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Following his own reasoning (consistent with his view elsewhere)
The set formula the Sages coined (literally, the 'coin' they minted)
Bills of divorce

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds that חכמים strengthened their rules like Torah law. He shows it in גיטין, and according to רב נחמן in the name of שמואל, also in requiring a חומש for תרומת מעשר של דמאי.

phrases.english: Yes, Rabbi Meir follows his own reasoning,
as Rav Hamnuna said in the name of Ulla:
Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַמְשַׁנֶּה מִמַּטְבֵּעַ שֶׁטָּבְעוּ חֲכָמִים בְּגִיטִּין –
phrases.english: anyone who changes from the formula the Sages coined for bills of divorce,
he must divorce her, and the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 by showing the ruling fits רבי מאיר's general rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing consistency (לטעמיה) with a broader stated principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seems too harsh to be real.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is רבי מאיר's consistent principle for any change from the formula of a גט.

steps.title: רב ששת's challenge from redeeming דמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a משנה where רבי מאיר allows redeeming מעשר שני of דמאי in easy ways, even silver onto copper and copper onto produce and back again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: One may redeem it silver onto silver, copper onto copper, silver onto copper, and copper onto produce, and then redeem the produce again, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say the produce must be brought up and eaten in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins a challenge to the idea that רבי מאיר strengthens rabbinic rules. He quotes a משנה about redeeming מעשר שני of דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי מאיר seems lenient with דמאי, allowing redemptions that he would not allow for real מעשר שני. Here it is the חכמים who are stricter. The next step builds the point by showing silver onto copper is normally not done.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
Redeem, moving the holiness from one item onto another
Silver coins
Copper coins
Produce bought from an unlearned person who may not have tithed

steps.confusionAlert: Usually רבי מאיר is the strict one here. In this משנה he is the lenient one, and that is exactly what makes it a challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
One may redeem it silver onto silver,
phrases.notes: "It" means מעשר שני money of דמאי.

phrases.aramaic: נְחוֹשֶׁת עַל נְחוֹשֶׁת, כֶּסֶף עַל נְחוֹשֶׁת,
phrases.english: copper onto copper, silver onto copper,
and copper onto produce,
and then he may go back and redeem the produce,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יַעֲלוּ פֵּירוֹת וְיֹאכְלוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: the produce must be brought up and eaten in Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from Steps 5 and 8 that רבי מאיר strengthens rabbinic rules.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of רב נחמן in the name of שמואל that רבי מאיר gives rabbinic rules Torah-like strength
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With דמאי (a rabbinic rule), רבי מאיר allows lenient redemptions, so he does not treat it like Torah law.

steps.title: Silver onto copper is normally not done
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת shows that redeeming silver onto copper is not normally allowed, using a משנה about a mixed-up סלע of מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can one redeem silver onto copper? But we learned: If a סלע of מעשר שני and a סלע of ordinary money got mixed, he brings small coins worth a סלע and says: Wherever the סלע of מעשר שני is, it is redeemed onto these coins. Then he picks the better of the two סלעים and redeems the coins onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת continues his challenge. He proves that moving holiness from silver onto copper is normally not done, so רבי מאיר allowing it for דמאי is a real leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the mixed-coin case, the holiness goes onto the copper coins only for a moment. Right away it is moved back onto the better silver סלע. This shows silver onto copper is not a normal way to redeem, which makes רבי מאיר's ruling in Step 9 stand out as lenient for דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Ordinary, non-holy property
Small (copper) coins
But didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: And do we redeem silver onto copper?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְשֶׁל חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ,
phrases.english: A sela of second tithe and a sela of ordinary money that got mixed together,
he brings small coins worth a sela and says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָהּ סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: "Wherever the sela of second tithe is,
it is redeemed onto these small coins,"

phrases.aramaic: וּבוֹרֵר אֶת הַיָּפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן וּמְחַלְּלוֹ עָלֶיהָ.
phrases.english: and he chooses the better of them and redeems it onto that one.
phrases.notes: He moves the holiness from the small coins back onto the nicer silver סלע.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מְחַלְּלִינַן כֶּסֶף עַל נְחוֹשֶׁת? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds רב ששת's challenge by proving that silver onto copper is not normally allowed.
steps.raayaObject: That redeeming silver onto copper is not a normal redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מעשר שני about a mixed סלע, where the holiness is moved right back onto silver
